title: Sunday Roast
subtitle: Braised brisket for 15
summary: Overnight-braised brisket with goose-fat roasties, Yorkshires, honey-citrus carrots, bay parsnips, cauliflower cheese, mash and proper gravy.

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.qty: for batter, cheese sauce and mash

tasks.text: Keep the butcher netting on all 3 brisket joints (about 10–11 lb / 4.5–5 kg total) so they hold their shape for neat slicing.
Season with coarse salt and black pepper, then sear hard in a hot skillet for colour.
Place the briskets side by side in a deep roasting tray.
Add 500ml beef stock, 1 sliced onion, 4 smashed garlic cloves and a dash of Worcestershire sauce around the base.
Cover tightly with a double layer of foil to trap the braising moisture.
Set APO to 80°C / 100% Steam (176°F), convection mode.
Slide the tray in at about 10:30 PM and run for 10 hours. A probe should slide in easily, but a slice should still hold together.
Cut roasting potatoes into irregular 45–50mm chunks.
Load onto Rack 1 (lowest shelf, elevated off the base), beside the brisket tray.
Raise APO to 85°C / 100% Steam. Steam the potatoes for 60 minutes total.
Remove the overnight brisket from the APO.
Pour most of the juices into a jug, but leave about 2cm in the tray around the meat. Re-cover the tray tightly with foil; the brisket holds in its own liquid so it stays moist.
Skim the jug and separate the golden tallow (for roasting) from the beef jus (for gravy).
Cover jus and tallow and put both in the fridge. Any fat left on the jus sets on top and lifts off easily.
Run the saved Cookidoo “Yorkshire Pudding” recipe.
Pour batter into a jug, cover, and rest in the fridge.
Rinse the TM7 bowl.
Scrub or peel carrots and parsnips. Cut into even batons about 2cm thick; halve thick parsnip tops so every piece matches.
Keep them raw. No steaming: roots soften too slowly below boiling and can set firm. Cover and refrigerate.
Drop florets into boiling salted water for 3–4 minutes.
Drain thoroughly and spread in a single layer over clean tea towels to steam bone-dry.
Run the saved Cookidoo “Cheese Sauce” recipe.
Fold sauce over the dry florets in a large baking dish; scatter extra cheese on top.
Leave uncovered 15–20 min to cool, then cover and refrigerate.
Peel and cut mash potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Submerge in a large pot of cold salted water on the hob, ready for later.
Pull potatoes: tip into a colander, rough up vigorously, spread on wire racks to air-dry.
Wipe any pooled water from the APO floor.
Switch APO to 65°C / 30% Steam (Sous Vide mode).
Place the covered brisket tray, juices and all, inside to hold until service.
Lift any set fat off the chilled jus.
Brown 1 sliced onion and 1 chopped carrot hard in a little tallow until dark and sticky (about 10 min).
Add a good glass of red wine and reduce by half before anything else goes in.
Stir in 40g flour for 2 min, then gradually whisk in the brisket jus and beef stock to make about 1 litre.
Add a splash of Worcestershire and the thyme. Simmer 15 min, then strain, pressing the veg.
Cool uncovered, then cover and refrigerate. Finish it at 1:10.

steps.title: Into the fridge, then go
steps.note: Brisket holds safely at 65°C in the APO. Everything else waits in the fridge: roasties drying on their racks, raw roots, cauliflower cheese, batter, gravy base and tallow. Go for a walk. Back at 11:55.

tasks.text: Once the steam has stopped rising, slide the potato racks into the fridge uncovered. The cold air keeps drying them for crisper roasties.

Put the fat in the Yorkshire tins and preheat to 220°C Fan. Use a layer about 4mm deep in each hole: roughly 1 tbsp (15ml) per hole in a 4-hole tin, or 2 tsp per hole in a 12-hole tin. Beef tallow first, topped up with spare goose fat or sunflower oil.
Take potatoes, roots, cauliflower cheese and gravy base out of the fridge. Give the batter a quick stir.
Bring the pot of diced mash potatoes to a rolling boil (15–18 min).
Stack 15 dinner plates inside on low warm.
Toss carrots and parsnips with olive oil, salt and pepper. Spread in a single layer across two trays, with gaps between pieces so they roast instead of steam.
Check the fat is smoking. If not, give it 5 more minutes.
Work fast with the door shut between tins: fill each hole only a third to half full. The batter should sizzle hard and the fat should well up around its edges.
Bake 20–22 min at 220°C Fan. Don't open the door.

steps.title: Whip the mash · second oven on

tasks.text: Preheat to 200°C Conventional/Circulaire.
Drain boiled potatoes thoroughly. Add to TM7 with butter, warm milk, salt and nutmeg; whip until silky (Speed 3–4, butterfly whisk).
Transfer mash to a covered dish and slide into the APO beside the brisket.
Pull Yorkshires to rest on the counter. Drop oven to 210°C Fan.
Slide in 2 large roasting pans with 200g goose fat (100g each) to get smoking hot.
Slide in the carrot and parsnip trays (raw). Roast 40 min, then glaze.
Carefully tumble the dry potatoes into the smoking goose fat. Roast 44 min.
Slide in the cauliflower cheese beside the roots. Bake 35–40 min at 200°C. It came from the fridge, so check the centre is piping hot (75°C) before serving.
Bring the gravy base to a gentle simmer. If it's thin, let it reduce for a few minutes.
Turn the roast potatoes in the goose fat.

Pull root trays out briefly. Test a thick piece with a knife; it should already be nearly tender.
  • Carrots: honey, orange juice, orange zest, bruised thyme.
  • Parsnips: red wine vinegar, bruised bay leaves.
Return both trays for the final 10 min glaze.
Season the gravy: 1–2 tsp redcurrant jelly, a dash of soy sauce or Worcestershire, then salt until it tastes rich rather than flat. Keep on lowest heat.
Pull roast potatoes. From Cavity 2: glazed roots and bubbling cauliflower cheese.
Switch to High Grill; slide in rested Yorkshires for 90 seconds to flash crisp.
Pull the brisket tray and the hot mash. Lift the brisket onto the board, snip off the netting, and keep the tray juices.
Retrieve the warm plates.
Off the heat, whisk a knob of cold butter into the gravy for gloss, then pour into warm sauceboats.
Carve the brisket across the grain, about 1cm thick. Lay the slices in a warm dish and spoon the hot tray juices over them so they stay moist at the table.
Serve roasties, honey-citrus carrots, tangy bay parsnips, cauliflower cheese and mash family-style.
Top with piping-hot Yorkshires and hot gravy.

lessons: 11 Oct 2026: carrots and parsnips steamed at 85°C stayed hard even after an hour's roasting. Now roasted from raw.
11 Oct 2026: brisket at 85°C for 12h was falling apart but dry. Now 80°C for 10h and held in its own juices.
11 Oct 2026: gravy tasted flat and slightly bitter. Now browned onion and carrot, wine reduced first, finished with redcurrant jelly, soy, salt and butter.
11 Oct 2026: Yorkshires rose like cake with 5ml fat per hole. Now a 4mm layer of smoking-hot fat.
11 Oct 2026: goose-fat roasties and cauliflower cheese were perfect. Keep as is.
